findings.explanation: The description claims an anomaly comparison against '-24h'. The SPL only counts matching lines over the last 24 hours, with no baseline, threshold or comparison, so any single hit alerts.
findings.quote: Surfaces Reconnect Failures anomalies for UC-15.5.12
findings.suggested_fix: Describe what the SPL does (counts subscription faults or authentication failures per pull-point and camera) and state the alert threshold. Add a baseline to the SPL only if you want anomaly wording.

findings.explanation: The SPL has no auth-failure field, and it matches 'http 401' only as raw text. Token rotation is not part of the detection and ONVIF device authentication does not work that way by default, since it uses WS-Security UsernameToken or HTTP digest credentials. The steps do not help build this detection.
findings.quote: (2) Alert on auth failures. (3) Automate token rotation.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe how the client logs pull-point creation, renewal and failure, and which log lines mean a failed reconnect. Remove token rotation, or state which credential type is being rotated.

findings.explanation: This sourcetype is not in the integration guide or any sibling UC. The text does not say what writes it, or whether `pullpoint_endpoint` and `camera_id` are extracted fields or placeholders.
findings.suggested_fix: Check which ONVIF client or bridge emits these events and what its log format and field names are, then document that source.

findings.explanation: A Universal Forwarder is not a Splunkbase app, and modular inputs generally run on a full Splunk instance or heavy forwarder. The wording is shared boilerplate across the CCTV UCs.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: Check what Splunkbase 617 is, and name the actual collection method.

findings.explanation: The validation step is generic and compares event counts to a vendor 'inventory count'. It never says how to provoke or confirm a subscription renewal failure.
findings.quote: Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`camera_id, pullpoint_endpoint`).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a validation that forces a failed renewal (for example by revoking the test camera's credentials) and confirms the row appears.

findings.explanation: Marked verified although the sourcetype and fields are unconfirmed. Nothing shows SME sign-off.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the status to draft until an SME has checked the detection against a real ONVIF event client.

findings.explanation: The URL contains an apostrophe, so it is probably broken. The ONVIF reference is the generic homepage rather than the event-service specification.
findings.suggested_fix: Use https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/SearchReference/WhatsInThisManual and link the ONVIF event service specification.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The pattern '(?i)renew|subscribe|disconnect|fault|http 401' matches normal subscribe and renew log lines, so healthy subscriptions will be counted as failures. It should match failure outcomes only.

summary: The description speaks of 'anomalies' compared against '-24h', but the SPL is a keyword count with no baseline. The SPL keywords also match normal subscription traffic. The implementation mentions token rotation without any connection to the detection.
